subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw add native framework-owned memory trust metadata and retrieval policy, or keep this as an external memory/MCP/plugin capability until a narrower plugin API gap is proven?
rationale: The issue is security-relevant and source-reproducible from code, but the durable solution changes trust authority, config, storage schema, SDK contracts, and plugin ownership, so automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design core trust contract first
options.body: Create a maintainer-owned RFC/API design for framework-assigned memory provenance and trust policy, then implement backend changes behind that agreed contract.

options.title: Route to plugin/MCP ecosystem
options.body: Treat world-model-mcp, AKF-style schemas, and memory plugins as the supported path unless a specific missing OpenClaw plugin API is identified.

options.title: Split into narrow prerequisites
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and prioritize narrower issues for source attribution, before_persistence_write, autoCapture filtering, and owner review gates first.

recommendation.title: Design core trust contract first
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-owned RFC/API design for framework-assigned memory provenance and trust policy, then implement backend changes behind that agreed contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest current-history owner for the memory host contracts, memory-core tools, and Memory Wiki/plugin seam that this decision would touch.
